audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart had every phases[N].side set to "Skill" while the content layer win[0..6] and the packet levelChart both read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri. Two layers rendered different answers to 'who wins Level 1'.
audit.why: Difficulty is genuinely even (50.93% over 428 games) but the lane is not flat: Neeko owns levels 1-3 on the E root into Q bloom, and Ahri takes over once Spirit Rush (140/120/100) gives her three dashes out of a 600-range, preparation-telegraphed Pop Blossom. The packet chart and the content layer already say this; only the full layer was stale.
audit.corrected: phases[0..2].side = Neeko, phases[3..6].side = Ahri, with phases[3..6].why rewritten to describe Ahri winning those stages and ratings moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes claimed 'level 6 adds the ambush; Luden's makes the package lethal' — it credits Neeko with the two stages the chart gives to Ahri.
audit.why: Level 6 is Ahri's spike in this matchup, not Neeko's: Spirit Rush is three charges of repositioning against a 600-range ultimate that has a visible preparation. Neeko's real spike is level 3 (E at 12s + Q at 9s) and her level-6 ambush only pays off with a disguised flank, which is a mid-game pattern, not a lane spike.
audit.corrected: Level 3 root-bloom is your kill pattern; her level 6 Spirit Rush takes it away and items do not return it.
sources: ownerKit R range 600, 'preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised'

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive numbers were absent everywhere. breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (defect 3), and no field stated Charm's flat 12s, Ahri's flat 7s Q, Fox-Fire dropping to 5s, or the 140/120/100 on Spirit Rush.
audit.why: Charm is a flat 12 seconds at every rank and is the single spell that starts Ahri's kill pattern; Neeko's E is 12s at rank 1 and is the only spell Ahri has to respect. Those two numbers being equal at rank 1 is the whole lane, and neither appeared on the page.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Charm 12s flat, Ahri Q 7s flat, W down to 5s at rank 5, Spirit Rush 140/120/100 against Neeko's own R at 120/105/90.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ahri's Orb of Deception deals true damage on the return and the page never says so; the missingInteractions feed flags 'resistances-invalidated'.
audit.why: Riot's own text: the orb deals magic damage outbound and true damage on the way back. Buying raw MR against her Q return is the wrong answer.
audit.corrected: Stated indirectly by keeping itemisation off MR and framing her Q by its 7s cadence rather than by resistances. Not asserted as a standalone new sentence because no existing field could carry it inside its length band.
sources: enemyKit Q text and trueDamage flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Essence Theft sustain (heal off 9 minions, larger heal off a takedown) is never mentioned; the feed flags 'needs-antiheal'.
audit.why: Chip poke into a farming Ahri is refunded by her passive, which is why spending E on chip is the losing pattern.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d rewritten to say the root is the only reason she respects you and that throwing it at a farming Ahri hands her twelve free seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed: dontsFull[1].d (title 'Spend the root on chip') carried the clone paragraph, and dontsFull[2].d (title 'Disguise-engage without R ready') carried the tradeBad string verbatim. dosFull[0].d (title 'Walk the clone at trade range as a decoy') carried the Charm-cooldown line.
audit.why: Defect 2 in the catalogue — the title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: All three bodies rewritten to answer their own titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ahri was addressed as 'he/his/him' in tldr, winCon, tradeGood, ahead, breakdown.early, breakdown.wave, dosFull[1].t, dosFull[2].t, dontsFull[0].t, report[0].t, report[1].t, report[3].t, report[4].t, report[11].t and report[13].t.
audit.why: champ-gender lists ahri as female; the owner is 'you', so every third-person pronoun on the page refers to Ahri.

audit.whatIsWrong: The most punishable cooldown was described only as 'matchup-defining' with no duration.
audit.why: Charm on a flat 12s means a missed Charm is a fixed, countable 12-second window in which Ahri has no setup for her burst — that is the only window Neeko's 120s rank-1 R should be spent in.
audit.corrected: Charm 12s stated in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[1].d.

audit.why: Whether Neeko's Shapesplitter clone blocks Charm as a projectile, and whether Pop Blossom's knockup interrupts Spirit Rush mid-dash, are both plausible and both absent from Riot's text. Neither was asserted.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood said 'the full package is half a bar at level 3' — a magnitude with no source (defect 6).
audit.why: No damage numbers exist in the kits; the sequencing is real, the fraction is invented.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the sequence and its real numbers: E at 1000 range, Q so the seed blooms again, auto for the passive, leave before her 7s Q returns.

audit.whatIsWrong: matchup-lint.js findings for this matchup: misgendered pronouns, Do/Don't bodies duplicating the generic trade lines, and/or a cooldowns field with no number.
audit.why: champ-data/champ-gender.js for gender; champ-data/_kits/<slug>.json for cooldowns, ranges and ability names.
audit.corrected: Pronouns corrected, bled bullet bodies replaced with title-matching content, cooldowns/magnitude claims given real numbers.

notes: Full-layer level chart was entirely 'Skill' while content win[0..6] and packet.levelChart both read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri — proposed as one atomic group (sides + ratings + the four whys that contradicted the new verdict). whys[0..2] already described Neeko winning, so they are unchanged. whys[3] additionally said 'Spirit Rush arrives' on the Levels 4-5 row, which is a stage error — Spirit Rush is a level 6 ability; rewritten to Ahri's 7s Q and Fox-Fire waveclear. COPY_PASTE_BLEED: Do/Don't bodies that were the generic tradeGood/tradeBad string pasted under an unrelated title were replaced with bodies that argue their own title, using kit numbers. COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT / UNSUPPORTED_MAGNITUDE: rebuilt around real cooldowns and ranges from champ-data/_kits.
